records.section_heading: Coral-associated marine fungi form novel lineages and heterogeneous assemblages
records.question: How did fungal community phylogenetic diversity differ between Acropora hyacinthus colonies from the warmer pool and the colder pool?
records.ground_truth_answer: Colonies in the warmer pool contained more phylogenetically diverse fungal communities than the colder pool and contained statistically significant 'indicator' species.
ground_truth_chunks: Colonies in the warmer pool contained more phylogenetically diverse fungal communities than the colder pool and contained statistically significant 'indicator' species.

Phylogenetic analysis of coral-associated fungal ribosomal DNA amplicons showed a high diversity of Basidiomycetes and Ascomycetes, including several clades separated from known fungal taxa by long and well-supported branches.

records.question: What sequencing platform was used for pyrosequencing the pooled PCR products?
records.ground_truth_answer: The 454 Life Sciences FLX Titanium platform.

records.question: Which analytic pipeline was used to de-multiplex, quality-control process, and cluster 454 reads into OTUs?

records.ground_truth_answer: Seven libraries were sequenced with 76-bp paired-end reads and four libraries were sequenced with 36-bp single-end reads.

Seven of these libraries were sequenced by Illumina Corp. with a 76-bp paired-end sequencing length (152 bp per sequence total) and the remaining four libraries were sequenced using single-end sequencing and a length of 36 bp in the lab of Dr Arend Sidow (Stanford University).

records.ground_truth_answer: The average BLAST match was 97% similar to the best reference sequence.
ground_truth_chunks: We found several groups in the Agaricomycetes, Ustilaginomycetes, Eurotiomycetes and Dothideomycetes that form separate, well-supported clades with branch lengths suggesting novel lineages (Supplementary Figures S1–S3).

The fact that our average BLAST match was only 97% similar to the best reference sequence of the commonly sequenced and slowly evolving 28S gene indicates a large degree of divergence from known species.

records.question: Did Symbiodinium genotype and water temperature have a discernable impact on the fungal community as a whole in this study?
records.ground_truth_answer: No. Within this study, Symbiodinium genotype and water temperature had no discernable impact on the fungal community as a whole, though they did impact the distribution patterns of some individual OTUs.
